verdict.rationale: Lago documents its own programmatic surfaces for agents: an OpenAPI 3.1 schema explicitly meant to expose billing actions to an AI agent, an official MCP server, and an in-product AI agent for plain-language billing management. Subscription creation (assigning a plan) and plan upgrades/downgrades are documented capabilities. However, nothing in the evidence shows applying a credit, shows that the MCP server can write rather than just access billing data, or describes scoped or least-privilege permissions for agents. Missing for 10: evidence of applying credits programmatically, scoped/limited API or agent permissions, confirmation that the MCP server supports write actions like subscription creation and plan changes, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate my billing — create a subscription, apply a credit, change a plan — through a programmatic surface with scoped permissions

citations.quote: Use Lago's OpenAPI 3.1 schema to generate clients, inspect typed operations, or expose billing actions to an AI agent.
The Lago MCP Server (Model Context Protocol) is written in Rust and provides AI assistants (like Claude) with direct access to Lago's billing data.
With our AI agent, you manage billing by describing what you need in plain language.
A subscription is created when a plan is assigned to a customer. You can assign a plan to a customer at any time
Customers have the flexibility to easily upgrade or downgrade their plan at any given moment.
